quest.title: A Herald Without Adherents
quest.description: After fleeing from those creepy ruins, you meet Dainsleif by chance. You follow him and begin your pursuit of the Abyss Herald through those ruins once more...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x650, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: So we meet again... a little sooner than I had expected.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, it's Dain!

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Judging by your expression, it seems you just experienced something quite strange.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Could it be that you encountered an Abyss Herald in those ruins?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? How did you know that?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I've been on the Abyss Herald's trail. I didn't expect to find you here as well.

choices.text: Actually, the Abyss Herald wasn't all we encountered...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: An inverted Statue of The Seven... holding Abyssal power in its hands? No, I have never seen such a thing during my time fighting the Abyss... though I have had my suspicions.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Tell me the rest of what happened in there. So you escaped the ruin depths filled with Abyssal power, and then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And then, as we got close to the exit, an Abyss Herald suddenly appeared and blocked our way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We fought a big battle with that thing. Maybe it hasn't gotten too far yet...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Yes, this is a rare opportunity indeed. Come, let's catch up to it.

choices.text: Yes, sir!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go! A rare opportunity! With Dain helping out, maybe we'll be able to solve more mysteries about the Abyss!

choices.text: Wait, I thought I was the one who commissioned you...
There was something even stranger than the Abyss Herald in the ruins.

talks.objective: Look for traces of the Abyss Order

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Those Abyss Mages just now... were they trying to ambush us?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: No, they were just digging through these abandoned Ruin Guards looking for something of value.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, is that so... The Traveler here seems to like doing that a lot, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looking for Chaos Devices, Chaos Circuits... You know, that kinda stuff.

choices.text: Yep, those are important materials!

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: They wouldn't be searching for such ordinary objects.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: In fact, I was nearby investigating precisely because Abyss Mages often come out from that ruin to explore.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: They seem to be searching the remains of Ruin Guards for a certain valuable object to take back to the ruins.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: However, they look disappointed, so it would seem they haven't found it yet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well then, why didn't you grab one of them just now and ask what they were up to?

choices.text: Yeah, Master Diluc's done that before...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I certainly don't mean to be merciful towards these monsters of the Abyss...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: But I have a feeling that their plan with this object is of major importance to the entire Abyss Order.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: One cannot discover the truth behind it through interrogation.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Or rather, these Abyss Mages likely fear something else much more than they do a painful interrogation...

choices.text: Fear...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Paimon is getting goosebumps thinking about all this!

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Alright, we shouldn't waste too much time here. Let's continue our search.

choices.text: Something related to what we saw in the ruins?
You should be rougher with them.
Abyss Mages probably weren't looking for stuff like that...

talks.objective: Look for traces of the Abyss Order

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? This Abyss Mage dropped a talisman... Could it be a communication of some kind?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Hmm, this talisman seems connected to the Abyss Herald. But why would an Abyss Mage be carrying it...?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Perhaps it really does contain information about their operation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, Paimon can't read the writing on it... *gasp* Is that the script of Khaenri'ah?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: #"...Engulf the faith of the enemy in flame, and bring glory to {F#His Highness, the Prince}{M#Her Highness, the Princess}..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wha—!? Is that what it says?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: "...'Loom of Fate,' initial operation."

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: They... the Abyss, seem to be carrying out a large operation. The keyword here is "Loom of Fate."

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: It seems like they are still launching the operation, or rather, are still conducting preliminary tests...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Loom of Fate"? What's that? Is it literally a... fate-weaving machine?

choices.text: The Abyss Mage came from those ruins...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: From the horrible feeling Paimon's been getting, those eerie ruins are super likely to be related to this fate-weaving operation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So Dain, what message does this talisman contain?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I'm reading it now...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Hmm... An ambitious operation, but some parts are difficult to understand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How so?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: In short, the first phase of the plan is related to Osial, Overlord of the Vortex.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Overlord of the Vortex!? You mean that god in the ocean?

choices.text: We weren't able to destroy it last time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do they want with Osial? Ohh...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Could it be the same as with Dvalin?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I know of your past heroics regarding Dvalin, and I also know of the Abyss Order's role in the Stormterror incident.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Though you may not have been aware of it at the time, you were thwarting an Abyss Order operation similar to this one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Last time it was Venti's old friend, this time it's a huge ancient god... The Abyss Order keeps setting their sights higher and higher.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Will the Abyss Order use their lies and dark magic to corrupt Osial, just as they did Dvalin?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: No... From the contents of the talisman, this operation goes one step further.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: They won't just corrupt Osial's mind. They also plan to use the ancient technology behind the "Field Tillers" to completely transform Osial's body.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is... that even possible?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So wait, the Abyss Order wants to make some sort of... Cybernetic Squid-God of Mass Destruction!?

choices.text: Sounds about right.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Very few people today truly understand the civilization of Khaenri'ah, though of course, the accuracy of that understanding itself is difficult to judge.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Only the Abyss Order has consistently sought out the remnants of Khaenri'ah. Despite being far from human, they seek out this lost human civilization quite persistently.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The talisman's message states that they will use "the Defiled Statue" as a base, attaching Osial's limbs to construct a mechanized god.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: And the new core that shall replace the orb usually held by the Statue of The Seven... is the eye of the very first Field Tiller.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "The eye of the very first Field Tiller"? ...Ohh, Paimon gets it! All those Abyss Mages are looking for this special eye, right?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: It would seem so.

choices.text: They haven't found it yet. We still have time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This whole thing keeps getting more complicated. But basically, it all has to do with that eerie Statue of The Seven we saw, right?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Yes. According to the talisman, the eye should be placed in the hands of the Defiled Statue...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Thereby imbuing the newly born god with the power to "topple the divine thrones of Celestia."

choices.text: (Celestia...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh boy... The Abyss Order sure isn't holding back with this plan.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm. Since no one knows where the first Field Tiller is, how about we take the information about the statue as the starting point for our investigation?

choices.text: That statue... It looked like the Anemo Archon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that Tone-Deaf Bard is too difficult to track down anyway. Let's go to the <color=#00E1FFFF>Cathedral</color> first and ask around, maybe we'll learn something.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The Cathedral... Hmph.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What's the matter, Dain?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Nothing. Let's get moving.

choices.text: Should we ask the Church of Favonius about it?
(Topple the divine thrones...)
Let's find the eye before they do.
These nicknames keep getting longer!
It was just crushed by the Jade Chamber...
Is it related to the inverted statue?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... Besides the Abyss Order, Ruin Guards sure are active around here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems wherever we find an Abyss Mage hideout, there's often a bunch of Ruin Guards roaming around too. Is that just a coincidence, or...?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: There are no coincidences in the world. Everything is the fruit of seeds planted long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Just like your appearance in that tavern... Time is just waiting for those seeds to sprout.

choices.text: But I only heard about you by chance...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Forget it. Just some needless musings.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The connection between the Abyss Order and the Ruin Guards is by no means incidental.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Rather, they are both branches that have grown out and up from the same roots below.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Branches"? "Roots"? What do you mean exactly?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Both originate from an ancient nation that was destroyed 500 years ago — Khaenri'ah.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Khaenri'ah!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really!? The Abyss Order and Ruin Guards are left over from after the destruction of that nation!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... Speaking of Khaenri'ah, that's really a super ancient name...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right. As your guide, Paimon should explain a bit here. A long time ago, the nation of Khaenri'ah was...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I know about Khaenri'ah...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Huh?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Because I have memories of Khaenri'ah.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You have memories of being there? But that nation was destroyed 500 years ago...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Is that so? Well, everyone has their secrets. You did not pry into mine, so I shall not pry into yours...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: But if you would like to tell me, I will listen... So, the Khaenri'ah you saw, what was it like?

choices.text: (Well, I can't hide it from him any longer...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's the complete story, huh... Paimon thought that you ran into that unknown god first...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: #I see... So your first memory after coming to this world was being awoken by your {F#brother}{M#sister} from within that meteorite...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #It seems your {F#brother}{M#sister} woke up first, but the question is, how long before you...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: #And then, your {F#brother}{M#sister} told you that the destruction of Khaenri'ah plunged the whole world into chaos and that you two should leave this world called Teyvat?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #"The destruction of Khaenri'ah"? {F#He}{M#She} said that?

choices.text: Correct.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: That destruction you witnessed, that's... history from 500 years ago.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: It seems the first time you awoke in this world was indeed during that period.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh... So your {F#brother}{M#sister} must have understood this world better than you did because {F#he}{M#she} woke up first.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: And it was shortly after that that you encountered an unknown god who blocked your path, so you couldn't escape...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon knows this part really well.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: ...I understand.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: When you awoke at that time and hurriedly tried to leave for another world, you didn't know anything about Khaenri'ah.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: But now, since you have come to gain some understanding of Teyvat, you are able to guess that the war you witnessed all those years ago must be the war that ended Khaenri'ah... Am I right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! If that's the case, you must've been flipping through all sorts of books during our adventure these past few months.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Before going to Mondstadt, you had just looked at some vague materials. Later, we managed to gather a whole bunch of old books from all around Mondstadt and Liyue, but you told Paimon they were useless...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #So the whole time you were just trying to learn more about Khaenri'ah so you could find your {F#brother}{M#sister}?

choices.text: It's the second most promising lead after looking for The Seven.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah... You can travel around the seven nations to find The Seven, but where can you go to find a nation that was destroyed 500 years ago...?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I probably know more about Khaenri'ah than both of you.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Khaenri'ah was a nation without a god — not because it had a god that died or abandoned them, but because it never had a god to begin with.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: It was a powerful nation built purely by humans, an unprecedented flourishing and glorious civilization — it was the pride of humankind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A nation... without a god...?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Later events unfolded just as you remember — it was all destroyed... by gods.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean that...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: 500 years ago, the gods descended upon the world and brought desolation to Khaenri'ah.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The "pride of humankind" was uprooted and crushed, like a weed removed from the garden of the gods...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How could that be...? The history books don't say anything about that...

choices.text: That's horrible...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Yes. Well, continuing to discuss the past now will only dampen our spirits.

choices.text: (But, the next time I see Venti or Zhongli...)

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Let's keep moving. I will tell you more of what you want to know as we continue our search.

choices.text: (I need to hear what explanation the gods have for their actions.)
#What a dangerous world... I need to hurry up and find my {F#brother}{M#sister}.
Despite only having a place name to go on.
That's what I heard at the time.
(Dain and Khaenri'ah... It's worth a shot.)
(The person who woke me up...)
(And that sea of flames...)
I don't really understand...

talks.objective: Look for traces of the Abyss Order

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Over there! It's more Ruin Guards and Abyss Mages.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dain was just saying how these ancient machines are from Khaenri'ah...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... did Khaenri'ah have a lot of ruins that needed to be guarded?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: No. "Ruin Guard" is the name modern people have given these machines. No one called them that 500 years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: These "Ruin Guards" were known as "Field Tillers" by the people of Khaenri'ah.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Field Tillers"? What a strange name.

choices.text: They were farming equipment!?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: It's not like you think. "Field Tiller" was just a code name. The people of Khaenri'ah liked to give code names to their weapons.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: "The land is not to be tilled with farming tools, but rather is to be fought for with steel and blood." —This is how the "Field Tiller" came about.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Fought for with steel and blood"? Well that's an interesting way of understanding "tilling"... Paimon doesn't think it's a very positive interpretation.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: After the destruction of Khaenri'ah, these masterless "Field Tillers" went completely out of control.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: They wandered aimlessly over the centuries, gradually spreading to every corner of Teyvat.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Perhaps resonating with the sorrow of other civilizations lost to time, they found their way to various ruins across the land, where they lie dormant.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds... so sad...

choices.text: Wandering aimlessly for 500 years...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Once you understand more, those details won't mean much to you.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: But no matter their past, all that remains of them now is the danger they pose... so destroy them all.

choices.text: It seems... we should put an end to their suffering.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... Paimon thinks you've been doing a real good job of that.

choices.text: So what's with the lethal weapons...?
